title: Best Tablets UK
short: Tablets compared using lab benchmarks, colourimeter screen tests and real-world battery drains, from all-round iPads to gaming, drawing and note-taking specialists.
intro: A tablet's real test is how it performs across genuine daily use, not a single benchmark number. This guide compares tablets tested by Trusted Reviews, who run colourimeter checks for screen accuracy, synthetic benchmarks for performance, and battery drain tests for office work, streaming and gaming, alongside using each one as their main tablet for at least five days.

products.name: iPad Air M4 (2026)
products.best_for: Buyers who want a confident all-rounder without a Pro-level price
products.key_spec: M4 chip, 12GB RAM, 480 nits measured brightness, Wi-Fi 7, 10-hour battery life
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this covers the full mix of performance, screen quality, design and software most buyers need, with an M4 chip delivering a clear step up from the previous model. Measured brightness of 480 nits held up in line with Apple's claims, and RAM has grown to 12GB for snappier multitasking, though it misses ProMotion and colour options feel a little drab.
pros: Clear performance step up from the previous model
Access to Final Cut Pro and Logic Pro
cons: Colour options feel a little drab

products.name: MagicPad 4
products.best_for: Buyers who want a large, genuinely portable OLED Android tablet
products.key_spec: 4.8mm thick, 450g, 12.3in 3K OLED at 165Hz, Snapdragon 8 Gen 5, PC Mode desktop layout
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this one of the slimmest and lightest tablets available, genuinely easy to hold for extended sessions. The 12.3in 3K OLED at 165Hz delivers vivid colours and deep blacks, and PC Mode unlocks a floating, resizable desktop-style layout when paired with the keyboard case, though fast 66W charging needs Honor's own charger, not included in the box.
pros: Gorgeous, high refresh rate OLED screen
PC Mode offers genuine desktop-style productivity
cons: Not the fastest chip for the money
Fast charging requires Honor's own charger, sold separately

products.name: Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra
products.best_for: Buyers who want a tablet that can genuinely replace or sit alongside a laptop
products.key_spec: 14.6in AMOLED, MediaTek Dimensity 9400+, DeX desktop mode, 11,600mAh battery
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found no other tablet can compare with this for a truly flagship experience rivalling the latest iPad Pro, with a gorgeous 14.6in AMOLED display giving apps plenty of room to spread out. The Dimensity 9400+ chipset made short work of demanding tasks like video and photo editing, and the huge 11,600mAh battery easily covers a full day, though it starts at £1,199 and takes 90 minutes to fully charge.
pros: Huge, immersive screen for work and play
Battery easily lasts a full day's use
DeX mode adds genuine desktop-style versatility
cons: Not the best benchmark results for the price
Not the most portable tablet around

products.name: iPad Pro M5 (2026)
products.best_for: Creative professionals who will genuinely push the hardware
products.key_spec: M5 chip, 12-16GB RAM, tandem OLED Ultra Retina XDR, 120Hz ProMotion, 12-hour battery
products.summary: Trusted Reviews called this the best tablet for creatives on the list, with a screen that's the best you'll find on any iPad thanks to a tandem OLED panel and 120Hz ProMotion for silky smooth scrolling. The new M5 chip handles editing large image files or cutting 4K footage without breaking a sweat, and benchmarks confirmed no other tablet gets close to its performance, though it's expensive and only a fairly minor update visually.
pros: Best screen of any tablet tested

products.name: iPad Mini 7
products.best_for: Buyers who want a tablet that fits in even the smallest bag
products.key_spec: 8.2in screen, A17 Pro chip, Apple Pencil Pro support, compact form factor
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this the device to buy if you want a tablet that easily fits into even the smallest bags, with the A17 Pro chipset proving more than powerful enough and apps launching in milliseconds during testing. Apple Pencil Pro support is a welcome upgrade for drawing, though the smaller 8.2in screen isn't as immersive for video as the Air, and it's locked to a 60Hz refresh rate.
pros: Apple Pencil Pro support for drawing
cons: Smaller screen less immersive for video

products.name: Astra 2
products.best_for: Buyers who want the fastest possible gaming performance in a tablet
products.key_spec: 9in 2.4K OLED at 185Hz, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, liquid cooling, 8300mAh battery
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found this pairs the fastest performance of any Android tablet tested with a bright, snappy OLED screen and serious cooling hardware. In benchmarks it beat the pricier Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra and landed close to the iPad Air, with liquid cooling holding 85.7% stability across a 20-minute stress test with no thermal throttling, though cameras are only fine and split-screen productivity is poor.
pros: Blisteringly fast gaming performance, beat pricier rivals in benchmarks
Excellent sustained cooling with no throttling
Bright, vivid high refresh rate OLED screen

products.name: Paper Pure
products.best_for: Buyers who want the closest possible experience to writing on real paper
products.key_spec: Grayscale E Ink screen, natural pen-and-paper feel, long battery life, no frontlight
products.summary: Trusted Reviews' top pick for note-taking, praising how single-minded its design is: every decision points toward making writing feel as close to real paper as possible. The grayscale E Ink screen produces high contrast for easy reading, and after a few minutes testers stopped noticing the screen entirely and just wrote, though some useful features like Convert and Share sit behind a subscription.
pros: Closest available feel to real pen and paper
cons: Some useful features require a subscription
No frontlight for use in the dark

products.name: Pad Go 2
products.best_for: Buyers who want a big-screen tablet without a big-screen price
products.key_spec: 12.1in 120Hz display, 7:5 aspect ratio, MediaTek Dimensity 7300-Ultra, 10,050mAh battery
products.summary: Trusted Reviews found the 12.1in display a genuine highlight at this price, running at 120Hz with accurate colours and solid brightness that holds its own against pricier tablets. The 7:5 aspect ratio suits split-screen multitasking well, and clean OxygenOS software with no bloatware feels fast and fluid day to day, though the chipset won't trouble flagship rivals in demanding games.
pros: Excellent display quality for the price
7:5 aspect ratio great for split-screen multitasking
cons: Performance isn't spectacular for the money
Main accessories are pricey additional purchases

guide.q: iPad or Android tablet: which should I choose?
guide.a: If you already use an iPhone, an iPad like the Air M4 or Pro M5 here makes moving photos, files and messages between devices seamless. If you use an Android phone, or specifically a Samsung Galaxy phone, an Android tablet like the Honor MagicPad 4 or Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra here will integrate more naturally with your existing ecosystem.

guide.q: Do I need a tablet with a high refresh rate screen?
guide.a: A higher refresh rate, like the 165Hz on the Honor MagicPad 4 or 185Hz on the RedMagic Astra 2 here, makes scrolling and gaming feel noticeably smoother. It matters most for gaming tablets and general everyday feel; for reading or note-taking, like on the reMarkable Paper Pure here, refresh rate is far less important than screen contrast and readability.

guide.q: How much RAM does a tablet actually need?
guide.a: For everyday browsing, streaming and light multitasking, 8-12GB like on the iPad Air M4 here is plenty. If you plan to do demanding creative work, like heavy photo or video editing, look for 12-16GB, available on the iPad Pro M5 and Honor MagicPad 4 here, to keep multiple apps and large files running smoothly.

guide.q: Is a specialist tablet, like one for gaming or note-taking, worth it over a general all-rounder?
guide.a: If you have one clear, dominant use case, a specialist device can genuinely outperform an all-rounder: the RedMagic Astra 2 beat pricier flagships in gaming benchmarks here, and the reMarkable Paper Pure's E Ink screen gives a genuinely paper-like writing feel a standard tablet can't match. For general use spanning several tasks, though, an all-rounder like the iPad Air M4 remains the safer choice.
